Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
544 AM CDT Thu Apr 23 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 

- A dry and warming pattern begins today.

- Hot and humid weather this weekend with heat indices near or
  exceeding 100F.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 128 AM CDT Thu Apr 23 2026

Low level clouds are increasing across the Coastal Plains, portions 
of the I-35 Corridor, and the Hill Country overnight through 
Thursday morning. Hi-resolution models agree on patchy to areas of 
fog developing across the escarpment through the same time frame. A 
few locations could see reduced visibility of 1/2 mile or less for 
an hour or two. Otherwise, a dry and warm pattern begins today with 
highs in the mid to upper 90s over most places and low 90s along the 
Rio Grande under mostly cloudy to partly cloudy skies. Later this 
afternoon, a few storms could develop ahead of the dry-line over 
west Texas and push to the east-southeat. Most model guidance keep 
the storm activity west of the Rio Grande, however, there is a 
slight chance for the storms to push into the Rio Grande and then 
dissipate.

For Friday, the heat is on with forecast highs in the upper 80s to 
low 90s areawide. Increased moisture in place with these 
temperatures translate to heat index values in the low to mid 90s 
for South Central Texas. Even though a dry weather pattern is 
forecast including a strong cap, there is a chance for some storms 
to develop as the cap erodes in the afternoon. The models favored 
areas along and east of I-35 Corridor and the Coastal Plains. And if 
this happens, there is going to be enough instability for those 
storms to be strong to even severe.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 128 AM CDT Thu Apr 23 2026

The upcoming weekend calls for dry and warmer weather across South 
Central Texas for the most part. When it comes to the afternoon into 
the evening hours, the cap could hold and nothing happen or could 
erode enough for storms to develop quickly. With that said, favoring 
the dry conditions through the period. The one thing we have medium 
to high confidence is about the heat that arrives over the weekend. 
Forecast highs for Saturday and Sunday in the 90s with heat index 
values near 100 along the I-35 Corridor and the Coastal Plains and 
exceeding the 100 mark over the southern part of the Rio Grande. So, 
the forecast message is that hot conditions are likely and we all 
need to make sure to stay hydrated and take breaks if working or 
doing any sports or activities outside.

The heat continues into early next week. Rain chances could return 
on Monday as a frontal boundary pushes across the local area, 
but models are not in agreement yet.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 537 AM CDT Thu Apr 23 2026

MVFR ceilings have developed at all terminals with IFR at SAT. It
doesn't look like there will be any further drop, but there is a
small chance for IFR elsewhere. There will be improvement by late
morning or early afternoon then all sites will be VFR through the
afternoon and evening. Low clouds will redevelop late tonight.
